QUOTE: "It ships one substitute, a buffer-based allocator. `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`library/memory_buffer_alloc.c:566`) zeroes the heap context and calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` to install its own functions." and "`mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init` is the only in-library caller of the setter that the index shows."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function as the only in-library caller of the runtime setter, installing its own functions over the pointers.
